text:
ConocoPhillips edged up 0.28% today to $135.02, a modest gain that follows a volatile week marked by a sharp 2.8% drop on November 23rd. The move comes as oil prices remain under pressure—US crude sits at $82.24 per barrel, down from levels earlier this month—but the stock has recovered somewhat over the past two days. The collapse of fossil fuel language in climate talks over the weekend may actually have provided some relief to energy investors worried about regulatory headwinds, though the broader energy sector remains caught between weaker near-term demand signals and longer-term uncertainty.

The gap between US and world oil prices (US at $82 versus global Brent at $91.80) suggests logistical constraints are supporting prices somewhat, which helps refiners and integrated producers like ConocoPhillips. Longer term, news around Latin America's energy resources and AI infrastructure buildout touching on oil and energy demand points to structural tailwinds that could matter for a major producer, though these remain speculative compared to the immediate headwind of soft crude prices.
